The camera is on the heather track at a standing woman's eye, two long strides from her, a 35mm lens. The low sun comes from the LEFT along the track. At the first frame the woman in the black straw bonnet fills the CENTRE of the frame from her bonnet at the TOP third to her gathered skirts at the BOTTOM edge. The shot is inside this place: Horsell Common with the sun going down in 1894: knee-deep purple-brown heather and dark furze, a stand of young Scots pines, a low raw ring of flung yellow sand round the crater a hundred yards off with a black band of heads and shoulders standing along it. The camera tracks sideways to the right, a truck with small amplitude past the hurrying woman, keeping the clerk and his bicycle in the right of frame as the woman catches her hem on the furze, hauls her skirts higher with her jaw set hard and comes on at a hurrying walk at a normal walking pace, and the clerk swings the buckled wheel round the same bush behind her, from 00:00 to 00:03. At 00:03 the furze springs back and dust lifts off the track under her boots as she comes on, and the lift continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:06 the camera is tracking through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
